rows: The system: lead-alloy type + oil-based ink + modified screw press + commercial book trade model
What is the type metal alloy?
Lead (~80%) + antimony (~15%) + tin (~5%); low melting point, expands on cooling for sharp molds, hard when cold
First major print run, c. 1452-1455, ~180 copies, textura Gothic type, imitated manuscript style
Water-based ink beads on metal type (hydrophobic surface); oil wets metal evenly, transfers cleanly
Adjustable metal mold for casting type; one dimension variable (width), matrix defines character; ~1,000 pieces/day
Why did Gutenberg lose his press?
Investor Johann Fust sued for loan repayment in 1455; court awarded equipment to Fust and Schöffer
Gothic script style Gutenberg used to imitate manuscript handwriting for market acceptance
How many copies of the Gutenberg Bible survive?
49 substantially complete copies; estimated value $25-35M+ each
